text: The QA sample consumes a rwb-decision contract that this Work Package does not declare: the closed-decision read that forms the population and the rule-row read of the version applied to each member. Both are consumed one hop with a 2 s timeout against that contract and its fake from Day 1, the C dependency on the rwb-decision contract is missing from the metadata of both slices and is raised at D1, and no decision and no rule row is read from a table, copied or cached by rwb-access.
why: TSD P4 v3 T5.2 names RuleCatalog and P7 as the calls a rule and a decision read goes through, so the target story cannot avoid the registry; the Work Package line for RWB-P4-E8013-APP carries C = RWB-P3-E1042-CON only, and the parallel E8007 slice of this epic carries the same omission. Root AGENTS.md rule 9 forbids inventing a dependency id, and rule 2 (P4 rwb-case owns the case list and the parameters) and R-PREC give no path to a decision or a rule on this side, so the reads are built against the contract and its fake and the missing C row is recorded.

text: The size of a QA sample and the tolerance the sample is judged against are parameters read through the rwb-case parameters contract (DP-06) on the run date. The parameter codes, the default size and the tolerance value are Not specified in the source documents (CG-B2-P4-013-1; ASM-B2-P4-013-2), so this story reads them and states them on the sample, holds no size, no tolerance and no default in code, and treats a population smaller than the size in force as a sample taken whole with the population size stated on the answer.
why: FSD P4 v3 A2.24.3.1 carries only VR-P4-024-1 and BR-P4-024, and BR-P4-024 states that no value a business person may change is written in code; the TSD P4 v3 carries no parameter row for a QA control; REQ-DRI-010 puts every threshold and limit in a versioned catalog. A size hard-coded in Java would break BR-P4-024 and the 100 percent measure of A2.24.1, so the value is read and the missing codes are recorded rather than guessed.

text: A QA sample and each QA finding are entries of the local decision-record chain of the DP-03 library. The record code they are written under, and the field-level shape of a sample, of a member and of a finding inside inputs_ref, are Not specified in the source documents (CG-B2-P4-013-1; ASM-B2-P4-013-3); they are fixed by RWB-P4-E8013-CON and by the library's own entry schema, the entries are append only and hash linked, and no entry is ever updated.
why: R-UNI-39 blocks an action whose entry cannot be written, and legacy RWB-E8-013 AC1 requires the result to be written to the decision log with the rule version, so the result must be an entry. The FSD and the TSD name no QA record code and no QA entity, the ownership map lists no QA table for the service, and the parallel E8007 slice writes its change entry under a record code it had to name the same way. Writing the sample as entries keeps the data model at the five owned tables and adds no table, which is what DP-01 and the ownership map ask of this service.

text: The QA sample's two writes require Rules and parameters C and its read requires R, as the legacy permission table of RWB-E8-013 states. The C letter is held by RW-COE today, and the primary actor of FSD P4 v3 A2.24.3.3 (the Conduct and QA officer, RW-CONDUCT) holds R only in TSD P4 v3 T6.1; the difference is resolved as a permission row and not as a code change, and the conflict is recorded as CG-B2-P4-013-2. The A letter of RW-RISK is not used by this gate because the gate performs no approval.
why: The role to permission matrix is data and is the only source of what a role may do (REQ-ACA-003), and the legacy table names C for the write and A for an approval the story does not contain. Refusing the control to its named actor for want of a data row would be a matrix gap, not a story defect, and inventing a C letter for RW-CONDUCT would invent a matrix value; granting it is a data change under FEAT-ACA-04 with no build.

text: The contract baseline declares the closed-decision read and the rule-row read as consumed from rwb-decision with the paths /api/recovery/decision/v1/admin/decision-log/entries and /api/recovery/decision/v1/rules/{ruleId}/versions/{ruleVersion} as placeholders, because no read source names them (CG-B2-P4-013-3; ASM-B2-P4-013-5). The owner, the one-hop rule, the 2 s budget, the error shape and the fake of each read are fixed by the document; a published path that differs changes one line per operation and a new version of the document with no change to a schema or a criterion.
why: The document must name something a consumer can build against on Day 1, and it must not present an invented path as a settled one. Marking the path as a placeholder keeps the contract buildable, keeps the drift test meaningful, and records the open element instead of hiding it, which is what R9 asks and what the parallel E8010 and E8007 baselines of this epic do for their consumed operations.

text: The sample state set is OPEN and COMPLETE and is this baseline's own, because no read source names a state of a QA sample. The document states that rwb-access writes both and writes no state of a decision and no state of a rule version, and the four legacy test case IDs TC-E8-013-01 to TC-E8-013-04 stay with RWB-P4-E8013-APP, whose criteria they cover, so the contract slice carries its own six contract test IDs and no second copy of the legacy rows.
why: Template and Rules R7.2 s16 fixes a Level column and asks a story to keep the legacy test case IDs of the criteria it owns; the contract slice owns no legacy criterion (acs is empty on its Work Package line), so restating the four rows would give one test case two owners and two Covers values. The state names are needed by the document and by the read, and neither the FSD, the TSD, the Epics 3 to 8 sheet nor the routing rules name a sample state, so the two values are declared as the baseline's and the gap is recorded.
